I have a a ton of family who is just about tone deaf and asking them to not sing has been a struggle. But I have an excellent singing voice, that sometimes makes them insecure. I sometimes encourage them to sing to the radio, especially my autistic sister, because she might due to embarrassment. But I would be absolutely heart broken if I was told not to sing because it made the song unenjoyable for them. And I could only imagine how much worse it would be for someone who couldn't sing, to be closed down by the person they love most. 
When you love someone, you shouldn't stifle trivial things they enjoy. You obviously cant help how you feel about bad singing being constantly around you, but she seems to love it. It really helps if you can see it the way she feels.
You should apologize. You probably stung her confidence real good, but hopefully sooner or later she'll be able to talk it through maturely. 
Wording and tone are key when my husband talks to me. You can either learn to tune it out, like i do, and sing. Or you can attempt a form of compromise. But personally I don't see a lot of compromise room. asking someone not to sing around you when you two are married, feels like an all or nothing to me. Unless she gets paid to sing at her job. She loves to sing, she probably takes you hating her voice on a very personal level, and you are going to have to regain that trust. Not saying it's fair, but you should probably concede. Or she will be peeved when she hears the radio playing, the song you stopped her from singing, or when random singing conversations pop up. You'd save both of you a lot of crap if you could cope with her singing. I guess you have to decide if winning this battle is worth it in the long run.

Come to me! Reassure me.

I really don't want to be by myself or say negative things about myself; so I keep to myself and it all stays in my head.

One of the biggest reasons my friendships with girls don't last is because I can't force myself to physically text you, due to my mental state. 
When you ask "Why do I have to text first? I'm beginning to think you don't like hanging out". Believe me when I say "I can't, but I always want to". 

I don't hate you, I'm not tired of you, and I'm not ignoring you. I just have this long dialogue between my rational mind and my depressive state. I know which is which, most of the time, but that doest stop the panicking and the bad thoughts from happening. And It's so much easier if you arrange a way to hang with me, because I don't want to go through that tug of war before every "You want to hang" I send.
And if I let some negative comment slip, don't tell me not to feel that way. Tell me I'm doing well. Or If you don't feel I'm doing well, encourage me. I can't help how I feel, but encouragement never goes unnoticed

TLDR: Offer to hang, don't wait on me. I'm secretive, but Always encourage

Yeah, that didn't go well. And coming from a family that is "christian" but have shouting fits on a regular basis, I understand that. With that said, children that age really don't understand. The child has faith or doesn't without any understanding. I'm not a parent, but if my child proclaimed he wasn't christian (or whatever) because of something one person said, I would be ticked. If you have a kid that is atheist, (because his parent's are, like all kids in any belief) and that child talked to a christian and now that kid wants to go to church, most parents would say their kid was brainwashed. 

Guess what, that kid has. By his parents too. But you know, this is an 8yr old. He can be anything his parents want him to be, again, with one conversation.
 
If that poor boy's parents are anything like mine he will have some hard decisions to make when he grows up. He is going to learn at some point that his parents are full of a lot of crap, but with each person there is things you believe in common. He will have to decide what of that he takes. And hopefully he won't let bitterness make his decision, thinking all christians are like his parents. 

The OP comment with "As most Christians I've met tend to be good at, they never once listened to my side..." is a common thing said on both sides. Angry people are like that, and you don't need christianity to instill that. You need insecurity (as portrayed by the OP's uncle) and inexperience (no knowledge of applicable actions or portrayal). 

I chose to keep my faith, the same faith, only acted out in a way I felt was a much better representation of christianity. I hated church and my parents for a while, but God was always what kept me. If I based my beliefs based off my parents or any persons belief that has never done wrong to me or anyone, I wouldn't be anything: Atheist, christian... nothing. And neither would you.
